texts: On day 380 of Year 2, Coraline Ash lit the lantern of the Harbor Station at sundown.
A crowd of nightmoths gathered at the Harbor Row.
Two sky-cats descended from the cliff-spires.
The two sky-cats hunted the nightmoth crowd at the Harbor Row.
The nightmoth crowd at the Harbor Row shrank.
The nightmoths left silken threads on the lantern.
Coraline Ash collected the silken threads from the lantern at dawn on day 381 of Year 2.
Hesper boiled the silken threads in sea-water in the second cauldron on day 381 of Year 2.
Mire-essence formed in the second cauldron by evening.
Hesper stored the mire-essence in a clay vessel.
Coraline Ash drew the stored mire-essence at sundown on day 381 of Year 2.

q1_issues.issue: The definite anaphoric subject "The mist-light" is filled by the bare kind symbol mist_light, which the parse also puts in class position (mist_light_genus), whereas a specific definite referent must be a typed witness.
"Mire-essence formed in the second cauldron" fills Patient with the bare kind mire_essence instead of a witness for the specific portion that formed.
The definite "the mire-essence" reuses that same kind symbol, so the stored portion is not distinguished from the mire-essence the lantern burned in sentence 2.
"the stored mire-essence" both reuses the bare kind symbol and silently drops the participial modifier "stored", which as a modifier is an adjective and licenses its own atom.
"left silken threads" takes Patient although leaving/depositing neither creates, destroys, consumes nor changes the threads, so the role test (and its unclear-case default) gives Theme.

Sentence 7's "at the Harbor Row" surfaces only as (LocatedIn sk_crowd_1 harbor_row), leaving the hunting event with no locative, though the event-modifier attachment is at least as available there as the NP-modifier one.

q2_gaps: A fictional-calendar date "day 380 of Year 2" — a day-of-year number with no month, inside a bare ordinal year: the Time section's (Day n)/(Year n) terms assume a Gregorian day-of-month and calendar year, and nothing states how such a date should be rendered.

An ordinal-modified noun with no associated ordering event and no explicit "-est" dimension ("the second cauldron") — Ordinal's scale slot is specified only as the associated event or a stated dimension, so no licensed filler exists.
review.notes: Event structure, compound decomposition, group/cardinality handling, the per-member distribution rules and the time atoms are otherwise accurate, and every head used is licensed. The systematic defect is that mass referents (mist-light, mire-essence) stay bare kind symbols even when definite, so one symbol occupies both class and individual positions and merges distinct portions across the passage.

issues.reason: Existential/definite doctrine states "Reserve the bare class symbol for a non-specific / generic object ..., never for a specific definite individual", so the definite anaphor "The mist-light" must fill (Agent sk_attract_1 ...) with a typed witness, not with mist_light, the symbol the parse simultaneously puts in the class slot of (Inheritance mist_light light).

"A bare plural in an episodic clause is a specific set, not a generic" — this clause is exactly a specific dated, located occurrence, so (Patient sk_form_1 mire_essence) asserts of the substance kind what the text says of one portion that formed in that cauldron by evening.

"the mire-essence" is a definite anaphor to the portion just formed, and the same bare-class-symbol bar plus "an anaphoric definite re-mentioning an already-minted witness reuses that witness" forbid filling Theme with the kind symbol that also fills the lantern's generic fuel object.

The bare-kind half stands for the same reason as index 2, but the dropped-modifier half is overstated: "stored" here restrictively re-identifies a referent whose storing is already asserted at top level (e13), and Coreference & anaphora resolves such a definite by symbol reuse without re-emitting the antecedent's atoms — exactly as "the two sky-cats" correctly re-emits no Cardinality.

Depositing threads on a lantern neither creates, destroys, consumes nor physically changes them, so the Thematic-roles yes/no test — and its explicit "when the test is unclear, default to Theme" — gives Theme; the same mis-slotting also rides inside e9_rule's (Patient (sk_leave $x) (sk_thread $x)).

An entity-attached "at" is licensed as LocatedIn ("LocatedIn is containment ONLY — in / at / inside / within") and the atom is true of the crowd, while Multiple live readings makes one reading the default and fires only on genuine equipoise — which the very next sentence's repeated NP epithet "The nightmoth crowd at the Harbor Row" breaks in favour of the NP attachment.

gaps_confirmed: A day-of-year number inside a bare ordinal year ("day 380 of Year 2") — the Time terms (Day n)/(Year n) are specified for a Gregorian day-of-month and calendar year, and nothing states how a fictional-calendar date of this shape renders.

An ordinal-modified noun with no associated ordering event and no stated "-est" dimension ("the second cauldron") — Ordinal's scale slot is defined only as the associated event or an explicit dimension, so the parse's (Ordinal sk_cauldron_1 2 cauldron) fills it with the comparison class, for which no licence exists.
new_gaps: No stated trigger for a bare MASS NP in an episodic clause: the "bare plural in an episodic clause is a specific set" rule is count-only (a GroupOf witness), and nothing says when a mass NP ("produced mist-light", "Mire-essence formed") mints a portion witness (Member sk_<mass>_1 <mass>) versus staying the bare kind filler that is licensed for non-specific objects ("burned mire-essence").

No licensed way to keep successive portions of one substance apart across a passage — the fuel the lantern burned, the portion that formed in the cauldron, and the portion stored and then drawn: the only mass-witness machinery lives in Partitives (a whole plus a PartOf portion of a presupposed whole), and nothing covers a portion brought newly into existence by an event or its relation to the kind symbol.
adjudication.defect_summary: Index 0: mint (Member sk_mist_light_1 mist_light) at "produced mist-light" and fill (Agent sk_attract_1 sk_mist_light_1), leaving mist_light in the class slot only. Index 1: mint (Member sk_mire_essence_1 mire_essence) and emit (Patient sk_form_1 sk_mire_essence_1). Index 2: reuse that witness — (Theme sk_store_1 sk_mire_essence_1) — keeping it distinct from the kind symbol the lantern's generic fuel object legitimately fills. Index 3 (confirmed half): (Theme sk_draw_1 sk_mire_essence_1) for "the stored mire-essence". Index 4: (Theme sk_leave_1 sk_threads_1) in place of Patient, with (Theme (sk_leave $x) (sk_thread $x)) inside e9_rule.
adjudication.notes: Compound decomposition, the group/cardinality handling, the per-member distribution rules, the connective-free narrative sequencing and the tense/time atoms are otherwise clean, and every head used is licensed. The Ordinal scale filler is filed above as a confirmed gap rather than an issue, per the reviewer's own routing.
